name: Applied Cryptography
description: Practical cryptographic constructions, attacks on deployed crypto, and crypto engineering.
narrative:
The earliest listed work shows applied cryptography at USENIX Security as fundamentally about attacking deployed systems and standards. In 2018 the headline results were break-the-real-world papers: "Efail: Breaking S/MIME and OpenPGP Email Encryption using Exfiltration Channels" (2018) showed that the two dominant email-encryption standards leaked plaintext through HTML rendering, "Return Of Bleichenbacher's Oracle Threat (ROBOT)" (2018) revived a 20-year-old RSA PKCS#1 padding-oracle attack against modern TLS stacks, and "The Dangers of Key Reuse: Practical Attacks on IPsec IKE" (2018) turned implementation shortcuts in VPN gateways into full attacks. The theme was clear: cryptography fails not in theory but in how protocols and implementations are deployed.

The next few years broadened both the attack surface and the targets. Hardware and microarchitecture became central, with "One&Done: A Single-Decryption EM-Based Attack on OpenSSL's Constant-Time Blinded RSA" (2018) and later "Lord of the Ring(s): Side Channel Attacks on the CPU On-Chip Ring Interconnect Are Practical" (2021) and "CIPHERLEAKS: Breaking Constant-time Cryptography on AMD SEV via the Ciphertext Side Channel" (2021) showing that even constant-time code leaks through physical and microarchitectural channels. Wireless and protocol crypto took hits too, as in "The KNOB is Broken: Exploiting Low Entropy in the Encryption Key Negotiation Of Bluetooth BR/EDR" (2019). At the same time the field's destructive side peaked with "SHA-1 is a Shambles: First Chosen-Prefix Collision on SHA-1 and Application to the PGP Web of Trust" (2020), the practical chosen-prefix collision that finally killed SHA-1 in trust systems.

Alongside the breaking, a constructive engineering track grew up: building practical, deployable crypto rather than only tearing it down. "Pancake: Frequency Smoothing for Encrypted Data Stores" (2020) defended encrypted databases against access-pattern leakage, and "JEDI: Many-to-Many End-to-End Encryption and Key Delegation for IoT" (2019) brought E2E encryption to constrained devices. The explosion of zero-knowledge and blockchain applications reshaped priorities, most visibly in "Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems" (2021), by far the most-cited paper here, which designed a hash function for the cost model of SNARK/STARK arithmetic circuits rather than for CPUs.

By 2022-2023 the center of gravity moved toward privacy-preserving computation and crypto that has to coexist with content moderation, voting, and contact tracing. Private set operations matured into efficient, deployable protocols in "Linear Private Set Union from Multi-Query Reverse Private Membership Test" (2023) and "Efficient Unbalanced Private Set Intersection Cardinality and User-friendly Privacy-preserving Contact Tracing" (2023), while "Identifying Harmful Media in End-to-End Encrypted Communication: Efficient Private Membership Computation" (2021) tackled the tension between encryption and abuse detection. Attacks kept pace, with "High Recovery with Fewer Injections: Practical Binary Volumetric Injection Attacks against Dynamic Searchable Encryption" (2023) showing searchable encryption still leaks, and new primitives like "SCARF - A Low-Latency Block Cipher for Secure Cache-Randomization" (2023) designed crypto specifically as a hardware-defense building block. The area today is a tight loop: deploy a practical construction, find a leakage or implementation attack, and engineer the next round of defenses.

milestones.title: Efail: Breaking S/MIME and OpenPGP Email Encryption using Exfiltration Channels
milestones.note: broke the two dominant email-encryption standards via plaintext exfiltration, defining the deployed-systems attack agenda

milestones.title: Return Of Bleichenbacher's Oracle Threat (ROBOT)
milestones.note: revived a classic RSA padding-oracle attack against modern TLS, showing old crypto flaws persist in deployment

milestones.title: JEDI: Many-to-Many End-to-End Encryption and Key Delegation for IoT
milestones.note: brought practical end-to-end encryption and key delegation to constrained IoT devices, marking the constructive-engineering turn

milestones.title: SHA-1 is a Shambles: First Chosen-Prefix Collision on SHA-1 and Application to the PGP Web of Trust
milestones.note: delivered the first practical chosen-prefix SHA-1 collision, ending SHA-1's use in trust systems

milestones.title: Pancake: Frequency Smoothing for Encrypted Data Stores
milestones.note: first system to hide access-pattern leakage in encrypted key-value stores with low overhead

milestones.title: Poseidon: A New Hash Function for Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems
milestones.note: redesigned hashing for ZK-proof arithmetic circuits, the most influential paper here and emblematic of the SNARK era

milestones.title: CIPHERLEAKS: Breaking Constant-time Cryptography on AMD SEV via the Ciphertext Side Channel
milestones.note: showed even constant-time crypto leaks through a ciphertext side channel in confidential-computing hardware

milestones.title: Linear Private Set Union from Multi-Query Reverse Private Membership Test
milestones.note: advanced private set operations to linear, deployable efficiency, representing the field's privacy-computation maturation
